British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values.
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain.
Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
• democracy • rule of law • individual liberty • mutual respect • tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome | Featherstone Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Featherstone Primary and Nursery School
Caring Ambition Respect Empathy
Welcome to Featherstone Primary and Nursery School. We are a large three-form entry school with approximately 700 pupils situated in Southall in the borough of Ealing.
We have excellent facilities housed in a modern building including large well-equipped classrooms, a library, ICT suite, and an extensive outdoor area including our Forest School, our 'Secret Garden', pond area, a large playing field and a wide range of playground equipment for the children.
Our caring, dedicated team of staff work hard to ensure that our children learn, make good progress and are happy and safe. Our pupils are very well-behaved, hard-working and enjoy coming to school.
We are a caring, listening school and have happy, positive, supportive relationships with our families. Our CARE values of Caring, Ambition, Respect and Empathy are very important to us all as well as our #FeatherstoneFamily ethos which we promote, encourage and demonstrate every day.
We are particularly proud of achieving the GOLD UNICEF Rights Respecting School Award for teaching and promoting children's rights. We are also very proud of achieving the Wellbeing Award for Schools (WAS Award) for promoting and supporting the mental health and emotional wellbeing of our children, staff and families.
Visitors are warmly welcomed at our school, so please feel free to get in touch with me personally if you would like to visit or find out more about our happy, caring school. I would be happy to meet you and show you around our amazing school.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
As they progress through our school and later life, we want all our children to be kind, caring, happy, healthy and confident individuals who enjoy their rights in full and experience success and happiness by embracing challenge, perseverance and hard work.
Ambitious for our learning
Respect everyone and their rights
Our Mission Statement
Keeping everyone safe, happy & learning
Our doors are always open to all. We are open, honest, and ask for help when needed without hesitation. We share and collaborate, work hard and make a positive contribution to the team. We treat everyone equally and with respect. We use positive language, kind words and respect to talk about and to each other. We work together to find solutions.
We acknowledge and greet each other with a smile. We value, care help and look out for each other. We are friendly, polite and go out of our way to welcome others. We create a warm, happy, positive environment and are thoughtful and kind to each other.
Vision and Values

pageCache.text:
Rights Respecting School
We are a Rights Respecting School
What is a Rights Respecting School?
A Rights Respecting School puts the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) at the heart of a school’s culture and ethos. This helps support our work on improving pupil wellbeing and enabling every child to reach their full potential.
There are more than 40 articles related to children's rights in the UNCRC, so our journey began by the school community identifying six articles we felt were the most important for our school:
In April 2022 we achieved the Schools Silver Award, recognizing that our children and the community are Rights Aware. We are now aiming to achieve the Schools Gold award in 2023.
Why are children learning about their rights?
A Rights Respecting School has a positive impact in four key areas of a child's social and emotional development:
Wellbeing Relationships Participation Self -esteem
We find that through a strong rights respecting culture our children:
Adults in school, parents and the whole school community also benefit.
How can parents/carers support their child to learn about the Convention at home?
Rights Respecting School
Are healthier and happier
Feel safe and cared for
Develop self-esteem and value themselves

pageCache.pageTitle: FAQs for Parents | Featherstone Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
FAQs for Parents
When can my child get a place at the Nursery ?
*The new term after the 3rd birthday.
How do I apply for a place at the Nursery?
Please visit the School Office and request an Application form that needs to be completed and handed in. You will need to bring the child’s *Birth Certificate or Passport and the Council Tax document for your *home address.
Useful Link –[add link to this info] the 30 hours full-time Nursery place.
What happens once my child is selected ?
The teachers from Nursery will send you a letter for a Home Visit to be carried out. This is so they get to know the child and the family, time for any questions you may have and more importantly, so the child is familiar with them for when they start.
What should my child wear to Nursery/School ?
Uniform is bought from an Online shop at www.stitchdesign.co.uk
GIRLS: Grey skirt/pinafore dress/trousers
Maroon sweater/cardigan/sweat shirt; School tie; White socks
Plain black flat shoes (not trainers)
Plain Hijab – maroon, white or black
Maroon/white gingham dress
Maroon sweater/sweat shirt
Black flat shoes (not trainers)
Plain Turban, hijab or Patka: maroon, white or black ONLY with no patterns or other decorations.
White short sleeved shirt
Label all of your child’s clothing and belongings - Please remember to write your child’s name (and class if possible). If we find any lost clothing, bags or other items, we can easily identify and return the items to you or the children. We have so much lost clothing and other lost belongings in the school without any names which all end up in the lost property boxes at the front of the school.
PE KIT (pupils can wear PE kit to school on their PE days)
What if my child prefers Packed Lunch ?
Please ensure your child has a healthy packed lunch, adhering to our communication [add link to this info]. They should hand their Packed Lunch to their teacher at Nursery or place on the Class Trolleys, for *Reception upwards. The Lunches/trolleys are taken to the Lunch Hall at Lunchtime.
What if I prefer my child to have hot school meals? What’s the process at this school ?
Initially, your child will be set up by the School Office and a password will be provided for you access the ParentPay system [add link to this info] that all lunches are selected and paid through. Pls ensure this is done before your child starts to avoid delay on their lunch. Any help can be given on navigating through this system.
For info, Nursery lunches are paid for per child in ParentPay.
Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 have free school lunches and are charged at 0 in ParentPay.
Year 3 through to including Year 6 are again paid for in ParentPay.
What if I have a question/s or query/ies for the School ?
Please come through to the School Office main doors and form an orderly queue to the *right/left side. Once the doors open at 9am and the Late children have been allowed through, our staff will come and attend to your queries in the queue and assist or direct you to the staff of expertise.
tart/End of Day timings & procedures from Monday 23rd May 2022
Start of day: School starts at 9:00. Gates open at 8:45am. All pupils must be in school and seated in their classrooms BEFORE 9:00. Any pupils arriving at the school gates at 9:00 or after, will need to sign in and be marked in as ‘late’ at the school office.
- ALL pupils/parents enter via the main gates (Western Road) then walk through the Reception playground gate by the side of the Nursery.
- Y5 and Y6 walk to and enter their classrooms via the KS2 playground fire escape. All other pupils enter via their external classroom door.
ALL pupils must be seated in their classrooms BEFORE 9:00.
EXIT: Parents/carers exit via the Nursery playground.
End of day: School finishes at 3:30pm. Gates open at 3:15pm. After 3:30pm, pupils will be taken to and can be collected as ‘late’ from the school office. Pupils must be collected by 3:30pm at the very latest.
(Nursery ends at the usual time of 3:45pm)
- ALL Nursery, Reception and Y1-Y5 parents/carers enter via the main gates (Western Rd) then walk through the Reception playground gate by the side of the Nursery.
- Year 6 parents can collect Y6 pupils from in front of the school office.
EXIT: Parents/carers exit via the Nursery playground.
Nursery - Year 4 can be collected from classrooms.
Year 5 can be collected from adjacent to KS2 play equipment (next to Year 4 classrooms)
Year 6 can be dismissed from or collected from in front of the school office.
Who can collect my child other than myself?
Up to *4/5 family/trust members can drop/collect your child to/from the school. All names MUST be added to a form that the *teachers will hand out at the start of the Class Year as it’s very important for each Teacher to meet all named members on your list. Our School takes Safeguarding and Security very seriously and will not allow a child to collected by someone not named on the form you’ve completed.
What’s the process for After School Clubs ?
New Clubs are communicated at the start of * September, January and April terms via a letter and email.
These are also available to select and pay via the ParentPay system. *You should select an £19 and £2 class. There are limited places per Club so once all spaces have been taken, that Club will stop being visible in Parentpay.
You should also complete a form for each Club you’ve selected and paid for with the *matching reference details from Parentpay and hand into the Class teacher or School office.
The paper and email schedule shows all the days each Club is active and days * (in red font) it’s not, which could be due to Bank Holidays or Inset days.
Clubs finish at 4:30 and ALL children should be collected from outside the MAIN School office.
What if my child’s class is performing in an Assembly – can I/we come to watch ?
Our Newsletters/Website will list the current and upcoming terms Class Assemblies. You are more than welcome to attend the *Morning or Afternoon Assembly times listed to watch your child perform.
Once all children have been dropped to their Morning queues, please form an orderly queue outside the Hall gates – the tall single gate before the school office on the RIGHT.
The teachers will allow access when they are set up and ready to allow parents to enter and be seated.
For those with small children, pls park pushchairs outside the Nursery building and take seats on the ends or further back, allowing you to leave freely if you and the child requires and to avoid too much distraction to the Assembly.
